newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian shares end higher, cigarette maker soars.
newsitem.headline: Colombian shares end higher, cigarette maker soars.

text.p: BOGOTA, May 9 Reuter - Colombian stocks ended mostly higher in trading that saw cigarette maker Coltabaco shares gain sharply in Bogota and Medellin.

Medellin's IBOMED general price index rose a solid 0.66 percent to close at 17,795.71 on above-average trading volume of more than three billion pesos. Bogota's IBB added 0.15 percent, ending at 1,173.05 on just over two billion pesos. There were conflicting accounts about the jump in Coltabaco, which has an estimated 60 percent share of the legal cigarette market in Colombia. Contraband cigarettes hold an estimated 55 percent of the market overall.

Some brokers attributed its new valuation to a pocket-to- pocket deal between two leading shareholders. Others attributed it to a ban clamped earlier this week on the sale of imported cigarettes in northwest Antioquia province, however. The ban could take some of the bite out of the booming trade in contraband.

Whatever the case Coltabaco, which is owned by the Sindicato Antioqueno conglomerate, rose 20 percent in Bogota to close at 3,865 pesos per share. It failed to match the gain in Medellin, but it led gains on that exchange as well by closing up 8.57 percent at 3,800 pesos per share.
Other gains were far less dramatic in Friday's trade and leading shares, including blue-chips Bavaria and Banco Ganadero closed slightly lower.
Banco de Colombia, the country's second-largest commercial bank in terms of assets, eked out a 0.7 percent gain in Bogota to settle at a discount to book value of 398 pesos per share.
